criteria.criterion: docs/design/async-drain.md has a section for each of the five points: read-ahead and hard-job planning; early producer start in its own worktree bounded by disk and shared build cache; one ordered landing queue with rebase-or-return-to-producer; CI waits and self-rebuild as background awaits; ordering of records commits with several jobs in flight.
criteria.evidence: Read the diff. Sections 3 (point 1), 4 (point 2), 5 (point 3: rebase, clean landing or a conflict returned to the producer), 6 (point 4) and 7 (point 5: one writer, Seq numbers) each cover one point. The content of section 4 has the problem described in the sccache finding.

criteria.criterion: The design states the measured baseline (median 42 minutes per landed job: producer 15, checks 13 to 15, landing about 6 to 8, verifier 2.3, reading and planning up to 5; 35 of 61 jobs landed over 2026-10-27 to 29) and a target in minutes per landed job with a stage-by-stage calculation; any figure not measured is labeled an estimate.
criteria.evidence: The section 1 table gives all the baseline figures, cited as the user's measurement, and 35 of 61. Section 8 works the target out: 14 x 1.2 x 1.15 plus 5 percent, about 20 minutes, with each assumed factor labeled an estimate.

criteria.criterion: The design gives a disk budget per in-flight job (with the arithmetic and the in-flight limit it implies), and failure and conflict handling: rebase conflict returns to the producer, a failed CI, a failed self-rebuild, a crash mid-flight, and a thrash stop.
criteria.evidence: Section 9: 0.1 + 5.0 + 0.3 + 3.3 = 8.7, about 9 GB, and floor((free - 20)/9) worked at 80, 50 and 35 GB free. The section 10 table covers a rebase conflict, failed CI, a failed self-rebuild, a crash mid-flight and the thrash stop, plus low disk, a producer timeout and a stale reading. The 3.3 GB sccache share is the item questioned in the sccache finding.

findings.summary: The design treats sccache as an active shared build cache, but D84 removed it (0 hits, per-job paths suspected) and nothing re-enables it. The disk budget, the recheck estimate and the cheap-producer argument rest on that cache.
findings.evidence: Section 4: 'D79 and D84 put sccache in front of rustc ... so the second job's crates compile mostly from cache.' docs/decisions.md D84 (line 1846): 'The sccache wiring is removed from athena.toml ... Re-adding the cache needs a measured cause first', and it suspects 'a per-job CARGO_TARGET_DIR and per-job snapshot paths' as the cause of the 0 hits. A search of every *.toml for 'sccache' finds nothing. The design adds per-job worktrees, which make those path differences larger. None of the ten build jobs re-enables sccache or measures its hits. A more correct design would state that the cache is off, add an early job that finds the 0-hit cause and measures hits across per-job worktrees, and redo the disk budget and recheck estimates without the cache until that job is done.

findings.summary: The 20-minute target counts every job as landed, while the 42-minute baseline is the end-to-end time of landed jobs only. The effect of failed jobs on the check slot is stated but not worked into the numbers.
findings.evidence: Section 8 charges 14 minutes of check slot per job and calls it per landed job. With 35 of 61 landed, failed jobs that reach checks also use the slot. The section says 'the cost per landed job is the same ratio' without showing the arithmetic.

summary: The change is docs-only and covers every acceptance criterion. It adds docs/design/async-drain.md with the five points, the user's measured 42-minute baseline, an estimated target of about 20 minutes per landed job worked out stage by stage, a disk budget with the in-flight limit it implies, failure and conflict handling, alternatives and ten ordered build jobs. It also adds D145 marked (proposed) and a CHANGELOG entry under Unreleased. The xtask tests and clippy pass. It still fails on one major soundness finding. The design treats sccache as an active shared build cache ("D79 and D84 put sccache in front of rustc"; "the second job's crates compile mostly from cache"). D84, which the design cites, removed the sccache wiring after 0 hits and suspected per-job paths as the cause, and no .toml in the repository configures sccache. The cache share in the disk budget, the 1-to-2-minute recheck estimate and the claim that early producers build cheaply all rest on a cache that is off today. None of the ten build jobs turns it back on or measures its hits. Three minor findings remain: the text says job 7 raises max_in_flight but job 10 does; max_check_slots is used but missing from the proposed config block; and the 20-minute target counts every job as landed, while the 42-minute baseline covers landed jobs only.
